elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (l) INSURANCE covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; no commercial general liability coverage or per-occurrence limit appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate CGL limit is stated; the new paragraph names only 'professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.'

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O is set at 'not less than USD 1,000,000', which is the fallback minimum and below the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Licensor hosts the Platform and processes Customer trade data, so the condition applies; cyber and privacy cover is set at USD 2,000,000, short of the preferred USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation obligation appears in clause (l) or elsewhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no certificate-of-insurance delivery obligation.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: New clause (l): 'Licensor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000'; Licensor is the counterparty alias, so the obligation runs the correct direction at the required amount.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Same clause: 'cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000' — matches the noun ('cyber and privacy') and the amount exactly.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: the inserted General Provisions paragraph (l) imposes an affirmative Licensor covenant for E&O of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy liability of not less than USD 2,000,000, matching both fallback elements in amount, coverage type and party direction.

The preferred level is not reached: CGL per-occurrence and aggregate limits, workers' compensation, and the certificates-on-request mechanic are all absent, and the E&O (USD 1M vs 2M) and cyber (USD 2M vs 5M) limits sit below preferred. Since the fallback level is fully met, the position is complete and no repair is required, but a drafter seeking preferred would need to add CGL USD 1M/2M, raise E&O to USD 2M and cyber to USD 5M, add statutory workers' compensation, and add a certificate-delivery sentence.

Minimality holds: the finding was 'missing', so a concise insertion of entirely new words is permissible, and the drafter omitted the model-language extras that are not required by the fallback checklist (at-its-own-expense language, the term-plus-one-year survival tail, CGL limits and the certificates sentence). No existing text was deleted or paraphrased — the retained Representation by Counsel paragraph is untouched.

Intent is preserved: the covenant is placed as a new lettered subsection in Article XXIV General Provisions, creates no undefined term (Licensor is a defined counterparty), no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the retained pass-through of insurance and shipping charges payable by Licensee, which addresses cost pass-through rather than coverage obligations.
